requirements.title: Round edit descriptors temporarily set rounding mode for real and complex formatted I/O
requirements.definition: RU, RD, RZ, RN, RC, and RP temporarily set input/output rounding mode to UP, DOWN, ZERO, NEAREST, COMPATIBLE, and PROCESSOR_DEFINED respectively; the mode affects conversion of real and complex values only for D, E, EN, ES, EX, F, and G editing.

pending.RU-sets-up: Future exact real fixture may use WRITE(buf,'(RU,F3.1)') 1.25 and expect '1.3' if 13.7.2.3.8 confirms the tie behavior; not executed here because rounding semantics are an unregistered dependency.
pending.RD-sets-down: Future exact real fixture may use WRITE(buf,'(RD,F3.1)') 1.25 and expect '1.2' after numeric rounding ownership confirms the rule.
pending.RZ-sets-zero: Future exact real fixture may use WRITE(buf,'(RZ,F3.1)') 1.25 and expect '1.2' after numeric rounding ownership confirms the rule.
pending.RN-sets-nearest: Source-control until 13.7.2.3.8 ownership states exact tie behavior and kind/approximation controls.
pending.RC-sets-compatible: Source-control until 13.7.2.3.8 ownership states exact compatible rounding behavior.
pending.RP-sets-processor-defined: Source-control: RP sets the input/output rounding mode to PROCESSOR_DEFINED. The choice of a processor-defined rounding result is not asserted here and remains dependent on the unregistered rounding-mode semantics.
pending.rounding-affects-real-complex-only-selec: WRITE(buf,'(RU,I1)') 7; expect exactly '7', showing integer output is unaffected.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans use independent literal expected strings or scalar sentinels. Negative plans change one property from a conforming control and attribute the violation to this unit only.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Pending output plans use internal WRITE to a CHARACTER variable and name exact expected characters including blanks when the unit is internally testable. Unnumbered prose restrictions are not promoted to numbered-constraint diagnostics. Where the source makes a behavior processor dependent, or where a rule requires external stream/direct/sequential files or unregistered defined I/O, the pending plan is explicitly source-control or unassertable rather than a fixture oracle. Real rounding depends on unregistered 13.7.2.3.8 and real approximation controls; RP is processor latitude and unassertable as one result. The RP facet records only the mandatory mode-setting effect; any processor-defined rounding choice is source-control/unassertable here.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies cited, not restated: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, and registered 13.1-13.4 for source form, expressions, intrinsic and character values, execution constructs, FORMAT syntax, edit-descriptor syntax, and format-control interaction. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: clause 12 data transfer, connection modes, effective items, and defined I/O; 13.5-13.7.2.4 for format item details and numeric editing; 13.10-13.11 for neighbouring formatting modes; clause 15 for user-defined procedures and defined I/O; clause 16 for NEW_LINE and IEEE inquiries if future fixtures use them; clauses 3, 5, 14, 17, and 19 where future fixture authors need terminology, lexical representation, IEEE arithmetic, interoperability, or scoping/lifetime controls.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, two rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_138.json. The reviewer re-derived the receipt (21 sections, 64 units, 0 hash mismatches) and INDEPENDENTLY RE-PARTITIONED the four crowded pages - p303, p304, p306 and p307 - unit by unit, confirming among other things that 13.8.8 genuinely owns only p1 despite covering six rounding-mode descriptors. A mis-attributed paragraph would have been invisible in the totals, since 64 would still be 64. The zero-numbered-R/C claim was verified: R1323 appears on p302 but belongs to the sibling 13.7.2.4 packet. FOUR blocking findings, all closed. C138SR-001: a negative was filed against 13.7.5.2.2, which only CROSS-REFERS to the rule - the actual prohibition is 13.7.5.1 p1 'On input, w shall not be zero' - and 'Note that w cannot be zero' is a reminder, not a prohibition; the facet is now an explicit dependency. C138SR-002: four units filed LATITUDE AS REQUIREMENTS - the fifth occurrence of the mixed obligation/latitude class, and notably the MIRROR of the sibling packet, which filed obligations as permission; all four were split into requirement and permission subunits. C138SR-003: an output-control facet sat under 13.9 p1, which owns only the input prohibition; output moved to p2. C138SR-004: a negative named a descriptor but NO DATUM, so nothing showed the p6 branch was reached; it now uses datum zero with (G4.1E3), where s=1 reaches the F branch, n=e+2=5 and w-n=-1, with repair (G7.1E3) expecting exactly '0.     ' - the reviewer derived all of that independently. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977.
